title: Cognitive Dissonance Theory Overview
text:
Cognitive dissonance is a psychological concept describing the mental discomfort experienced by a person who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values. This discomfort arises when an individual's behavior contradicts their deeply held attitudes, creating an internal tension that motivates the need for resolution.

The theory posits that to alleviate this unpleasant state of inconsistency, the individual will naturally attempt to modify one of the conflicting cognitions, introduce a new consistent cognition, or minimize the importance of the discrepancy. For example, believing strongly in environmental conservation while driving frequently in a gas-guzzling vehicle creates dissonance, which might be reduced by downplaying the impact of personal driving habits.

Understanding this process is crucial for analyzing human decision-making and belief systems, as it explains the tendency toward self-justification even when presented with compelling contradictory evidence.
